episodes.202832: The monsoon high that was over the state the earlier in the week, moved west over western Arizona and southern California on July 10th in response to an upper level trough moving across the northern and central Rockies. This resulted in the development of severe thunderstorms across the northeast and east central plains ahead of the trough axis during the afternoon and evening hours. Additionally, a drier thunderstorm resulted in a high wind gust at a mesonet station on the White Sand Missile range. Storms weakened around sunset due to the loss of daytime heating as they continued moving south into southeast New Mexico. Another round of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a dryline across the east slopes of the central mountain chain during the afternoon hours on July 11th. Storms across the east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains congealed into a line of severe storms across the northeast and east central plains during the mid evening hours bringing severe thunderstorm wind gusts of up to 77 mph at various stations across Quay County. This line of storms exited into West Texas with additional redevelopment across the east central and southeast plains during the early morning hours of July 12th.||Outflow from these late night and early morning storms pushed a backdoor front and higher surface moisture behind the front west through the gaps of the central mountain and to the Continental Divide in western New Mexico setting the stage for shower and thunderstorm activity across central New Mexico during the afternoon and evening hours on July 12th. Intense severe thunderstorms across the Sandia Mountains and East Mountain communities resulted in hail up to golf ball size along with flash flooding in the Tijeras Arroyo, Arroyo de San Antonio and other low water crossings in the area due to rainfall amounts of up to 3 inches. Gusty outflow winds from storms to the north and east resulted in a 66 mph wind gust at the Albuquerque Sunport.
episodes.202875: Multiple clusters of strong thunderstorms developed during peak afternoon heating across north Alabama. A couple of these thunderstorms produced gust front outflows which knocked down a tree or tree limb at a few locations.
episodes.202895: A moist and unstable summer airmass led to the development of scattered afternoon thunderstorms, a few of which were strong to severe.
episodes.202915: A developing thunderstorm produced a weak, brief landspout tornado southeast of Aberdeen.
episodes.202916: A thunderstorm produced high winds and wind related damage to trees and crops west of the town of Barry. A peak wind gust of 61 mph was measured by a roof top anemometer 2 miles north northwest of Barry. Multiple large limbs were observed broken while several smaller trees were snapped just off the ground.
episodes.202934: A weak cold front slowly moved across northern NY during the afternoon and evening hours of July 13th. Several rounds of tropical showers and thunderstorms traversed the area with a few storms pulsing to severe limits. In addition, localized heavy rainfall caused flash flooding in the form of a landslide.
episodes.203029: Showers and thunderstorms developed early in the afternoon in an anomalously moist airmass along the Chesapeake Bay Breeze and remnant outflow boundaries. These storms remained nearly stationary through the first part of the afternoon producing a quick two to four inches of rain before dissipating.
episodes.203031: Showers and thunderstorms developed early in the afternoon in an anomalously moist airmass along the Chesapeake Bay Breeze and remnant outflow boundaries. These storms remained nearly stationary through the first part of the afternoon producing a quick two to four inches of rain before dissipating.
episodes.203032: Showers and thunderstorms developed early in the afternoon in an anomalously moist airmass along the Chesapeake Bay Breeze and remnant outflow boundaries. These storms remained nearly stationary through the first part of the afternoon producing a quick two to four inches of rain before dissipating.
episodes.203070: A shortwave trough, moving through an unstable and extremely moist air mass (PWATs over 2.00) over central Pennsylvania, allowed for showers and thunderstorms to develop across the area during the afternoon hours of July 13, 2025. Thunderstorms in this environment began to become strong-to-severe; however, rainfall rates within the thunderstorms were the most notable feature, topping out over two inches per hour. The slow movement of these thunderstorms produced instances of flooding and flash flooding in York County, mainly stationed around Dover where Fox Run went over its banks and water rescues were reported. Showers and thunderstorms continued into the evening hours, where storms become anchored to higher elevation locations in Lycoming and Sullivan counties. Multiple roadways in Sullivan County were closed due to flooding and mudslides, with the nearby town of Glen Mawr (Lycoming County) being placed under a mandatory evacuation as Muncy Creek rose 10 feet in three to four hours. Flooding concerns across Sullivan and Lycoming County continued into the early morning hours of July 14, 2025 as rain began to taper off across the area.
episodes.203401: An upper level trough over Eastern Oklahoma and North Texas was wedged between an upper level ridge of high pressure over the Southern Great Basin and the Northeast Gulf during the afternoon of July 13th. Ample gulf moisture was present during the afternoon, and contributed to strong instability as temperatures climbed into the mid 90s across East Texas. Despite the weak wind shear in place, scattered severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon which became outflow dominant, resulting in instances of damaging winds which downed trees and power lines during the late afternoon hours before diminishing with the loss of daytime heating.
episodes.203402: An upper level trough over Eastern Oklahoma and North Texas was wedged between an upper level ridge of high pressure over the Southern Great Basin and the Northeast Gulf during the afternoon of July 13th. Ample gulf moisture was present during the afternoon, and contributed to strong instability as temperatures climbed into the mid 90s across Western Louisiana. Despite the weak wind shear in place, scattered severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon which became outflow dominant, resulting in instances of damaging winds which downed trees and power lines during the late afternoon hours across Caddo and Sabine Parishes before diminishing with the loss of daytime heating.
episodes.203749: Scattered thunderstorms were supported by an unstable environment. Shear was weak, so most storms stayed sub-severe. However, one storm did become severe as it moved across the Mohawk Valley and Tug Hill Plateau. Strong gusts with this storm knocked down a tree onto a roadway. Otherwise, most reports this day were related to heavy rain.
episodes.203940: A hot and humid air mass combined with orographical lift to produce a severe thunderstorm in Franklin County of southwest Virginia. Damaging wind gusts from this storm blew down three trees and a couple large branches about six miles north-northwest of Burnt Chimney.
episodes.204086: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours with a weak trough passage. Sufficient destabilization up to 2000 J/kg MLCAPE with weak flow and 900-1100 J/kg of DCAPE was enough for stronger thunderstorms to produce downbursts with damaging wind.
episodes.204623: A surface front shifted southward across north Florida with moist SW from the Gulf and a dominant west coast sea breeze regime triggering scattered storm pulse storms.
episodes.204674: Isolated storms developed in the afternoon over the northeast Piedmont and Coastal Plain in a warm and humid airmass. The storms then drifted slowly west and southwest in the evening hours over the Piedmont and Sandhills. Some isolated wind damage and flash flood reports were observed.
episodes.204780: Upslope flow, coupled with disturbances in the northerly flow aloft, resulted in the development of thunderstorms in far West Texas and portions of Southeast New Mexico. One of these storms produced a severe wind gust at Castolon.
episodes.204853: The tail end of an upper level trough moving through the Upper Midwest was affecting the Sacramento Mountains.  Modest moisture at the low levels added to the instability across the area which resulted in strong thunderstorms with a lot of hail and flash flooding in the Sacramentos.
episodes.205006: Thunderstorms formed along an outflow boundary in a moist airmass over Central Texas and moved into the Hill Country and Edwards Plateau. Some of these storms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.205033: An upper trough moving out of the Southern Plains combined with afternoon heating to produce scattered thunderstorms. A moist airmass with precipitable water values around 2 inches led to a couple of wet microbursts that produced damaging winds across DeSoto County.
episodes.205122: A moist and unstable summer airmass led to the development of scattered afternoon thunderstorms, a few of which were strong to severe.
episodes.205293: A moist and unstable air mass resulted in scattered storms developing across portions of central and eastern Virginia on July 13. These slow-moving storms produced heavy rainfall and flash flooding, especially across the Tri-Cities.
episodes.205430: A slow moving isolated thunderstorm produced flooding.
episodes.205579: Scattered showers and thunderstorms tracked east-northeastward across the Quad State during the day as a very slow moving front was set up from the WSW to ENE across northern portions of the Quad State. The strongest cluster of storms was during the afternoon in the Southern Pennyrile which produced multiple reports of damage in Hopkinsville. MLCAPE values were over 2000J/kg with DCAPE highest in the Pennyrile at around 800J/kg late afternoon. Shear was limited, helping to keep severe weather potential limited.
episodes.205906: The combination of pre-frontal trough, deep moisture and increased instability resulted in the development of showers and thunderstorms on the afternoon of July 13. Thunderstorms stretch from the western Southern Tier to the North Country. At times the thunderstorms became strong to severe with gusty winds and heavy rainfall.
episodes.205946: A warm and unstable environment ahead of an approaching cold front supported the development of scattered thunderstorms. Weak steering winds contributed to slow moving storms repeating over the same areas which contributed to areas of heavy rainfall and flash flooding. Several locations around central New York reported flooded roads along with washouts of culverts and small bridges.
episodes.206083: The combination of deep tropical moisture and a weak upper level area of low pressure produced heavy rainfall and flash flooding across portions of the Northwest Hill Country and Heartland.
episodes.206088: Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms occurred the weekend of July 12, influenced by remnant outflow boundaries, a stalled front, and a slow-moving upper low. A mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) further enhanced precipitation totals and rain rates, resulting in flash flooding primarily across Central Texas.
episodes.206108: A line of severe thunderstorms moving southwestward from the Arizona and New Mexico border sent a dust storm, or haboob, through Cochise county. There were numerous reports of less than 0.25 mile visibility due to dust and a crash on I-10 due to the reduced visibility.
episodes.206194: Thunderstorms moved across southeast Louisiana on July 13, 2025, producing strong winds over Lake Pontchartrain. A mesonet station in Eden Isle measured a gust of 41 mph (36 kt) during one of the storms.
episodes.206310: Weak northwesterly flow was in place over the area, which allowed for scattered storms to develop across south central Colorado. A couple of these storms became severe.
episodes.206328: Thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts near Sanford and Cape Canaveral.
episodes.206329: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms produced strong to severe wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.206413: Strong to severe sea breeze thunderstorms developed near Lake Okeechobee and inland Southwest Florida on the afternoon and evening of July 13, 2025.
episodes.206730: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms produced occasionally severe wind gusts across parts of Mississippi.
episodes.207959: Scattered thunderstorms developed over Lake Michigan on the evening of the 12th and continued to track eastward into Lower Michigan producing mainly heavy rain and some localized street flooding in Traverse City.

events.narrative: A spotter observed nickel size hail accumulations of 6 to 8 inches deep from a severe thunderstorm. The hail resulted in widespread damage to vegetation, homes, and vehicles.

Heavy rain from slow moving severe thunderstorms resulted in severe flash flooding in the East Mountain communities of Cedar Crest, Tijeras and Sedillo. A 300 pound woodchipper was carried downstream on the normally dry Arroyo de San Antonio until becoming lodged in a tree. Video taken by a viewer in Tijeras and shared by a broadcast meteorologist shows Tijeras Arroyo flowing out of banks. A small tree was also moving downstream in the arroyo. Spotters also observed flood waters flowing down hillsides around Tijeras, Tablazon, and Zuzax with hail, rocks, mud, and debris covering parts of SR-333. Finally, low water crossings were completely flooded on secondary roads just east and south of the Zuzax exit at I-40.
